pr.body:
## Summary This pull request introduces a new feature to manage calendar cache data, including the ability to view cache status and delete cached data. It also includes several supporting updates to repositories, APIs, and UI components. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme. ### New Feature: Calendar Cache Management * Added a `deleteCache` mutation to the TRPC `calendarsRouter`, enabling users to delete cached calendar data by credential ID. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsxR27-R33](diffhunk://#diff-9e053175cc6dfb5717313e0587a730fff132f9d3c1200204f0ce8dac53a19280R27-R33)`) * Introduced the `deleteCacheHandler` to handle cache deletion logic, including validation of user access to the specified credential. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.tsR1-R33](diffhunk://#diff-572888b8e0555167a5787847f29d5a46623eff170491acc0654e916f5b4afd18R1-R33)`) * Updated the `connectedCalendarsHandler` to enrich calendar data with cache status (`cacheUpdatedAt`) by querying the `CalendarCacheRepository`. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.tsR27-R39](diffhunk://#diff-3f6a556ad60f26d0162770fcd81b5bddeb6ab0437552ac792045c3cd2608d710R27-R39)`) ### UI Enhancements * Created a new `CredentialActionsDropdown` component to display cache status and provide options to delete cached data or disconnect integrations. (`[packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsxR1-R134](diffhunk://#diff-c78273434b95ab8276bb5eb24d9bc088b10af029388bdcd08cbe478f44269b31R1-R134)`) * Replaced the `DisconnectIntegration` component with `CredentialActionsDropdown` in the `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` UI, integrating the new cache management functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L5-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L70-L81)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L125-L135)`) ### Repository and Database Updates * Added a `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method to the `CalendarCacheRepository` and its mock implementation to fetch cache statuses for multiple credentials. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b36c72c0db751ba0cafe234dfa150817672869825333c22b074c4977a6135b8dR30-R32)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ceffbae9ef3da413495feac73a341672e77ffaf493cf67ada0b637ead80ded38R26-R30)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4cf8d3089fad7b6c8fe4172d8d42147f136b65baf30b726e57b9b10d179d4a99R172-R188)`) * Introduced a new `updateManyByCredentialId` method in the `SelectedCalendarRepository` to update multiple calendars by credential ID. (`[packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.tsR400-R406](diffhunk://#diff-ccb4eecfa701e5b0c7d6ba87dcc550cdf3700a63ee252849045611599ecb9273R400-R406)`) * Added an `updatedAt` column to the `CalendarCache` table in the database schema and Prisma model to track the last update timestamp. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f597bd98bbcfdcf4861ee7bf0c238e7dfe54b456ceb69b852aaf3979c4102cfR1-R8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-56fa4d384ba6fb94b130e9eb42c5cad00734b025ebd6c197f76873469725ae87R1718)`) ### Localization and Strings * Added new localization strings for cache management actions, such as "Cache Status," "Delete cached data," and "Cache deleted successfully." (`[apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.jsonR3376-R3382](diffhunk://#diff-57de4b8e5231f1d699891d98b0381d56e9e24537b0ca5420d1fba4f0597370bcR3376-R3382)`) ### Miscellaneous * Updated `package.json` to replace `ts-node` with `npx tsx` for running the `dev:cron` script. (`[apps/web/package.jsonL11-R11](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L11-R11)`) ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human **🔴 High Priority (5 items)** - [x] **Verify deleteCache tRPC mutation exists** - The component references `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache.useMutation()` but this mutation implementation is not visible in the PR changes. Check if this endpoint exists or needs to be created. - [x] **End-to-end testing with Google Calendar** - Install a Google Calendar integration and verify the credential-level dropdown appears, shows cache status, and deletion flow works correctly with confirmation dialog. - [x] **Test cache status display logic** - Verify that `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamps are correctly formatted and displayed only for Google Calendar credentials with actual cache data. - [x] **Confirm repository pattern correctness** - Test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` returns accurate data and the credential-to-cache mapping works properly in the UI. - [x] **Verify dropdown conditional rendering** - Ensure the dropdown only appears for Google Calendar credentials and handles edge cases (no cache, disabled integrations, etc.). **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Connect a Google Calendar integration to trigger cache creation 2. Navigate to `/apps/installed/calendar` 3. Verify dropdown appears on Google Calendar credential with cache status and timestamp 4. Test "Delete cached data" action shows confirmation dialog 5. Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately 6. Test "Remove App" functionality still works correctly --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD UI["CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx
(New Component)"]:::major-edit Handler["connectedCalendars.handler.ts
(Updated tRPC Handler)"]:::major-edit RepoInterface["calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts
(Updated Interface)"]:::minor-edit RepoImpl["calendar-cache.repository.ts
(Updated Implementation)"]:::minor-edit RepoMock["calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts
(Updated Mock)"]:::minor-edit Translations["common.json
(Added Translation Keys)"]:::minor-edit UI -->|"Uses repository via tRPC"| Handler Handler -->|"Calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds"| RepoImpl RepoImpl -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface RepoMock -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface UI -->|"Uses translation keys"| Translations subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - **Session Details**: Requested by @zomars, implemented in Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/24545e0980df465995521419432a2a52 - **SelectedCalendar.updatedAt Usage**: Currently only updated in backend via Google webhook handler but not displayed in frontend. Frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Consider if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update should be removed. - **Import Path Resolution**: Had to fix UI component import paths during development - watch for potential module resolution issues in different environments. - **Testing Limitation**: Local testing was limited due to no installed calendar integrations - end-to-end verification with real Google Calendar data is essential.

raw_findings.body: The actions menu offers Remove app for a credential that cannot be disconnected through the credentials API, causing a failed removal attempt and exposing an invalid destructive action.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The UI permits an unsupported credential mutation instead of hiding the disconnect action.
raw_findings.impact: The actions menu offers Remove app for a credential that cannot be disconnected through the credentials API, causing a failed removal attempt and exposing an invalid destructive action.
raw_findings.root_cause: The replacement component dropped the existing synthetic/in-memory delegation credential check and only checks the optional relation ID.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Also require `!isDelegationCredential({ credentialId })` when computing `canDisconnect`, as the replaced DisconnectIntegration component did.
raw_findings.title: Preserve the in-memory delegation credential disconnect guard
raw_findings.trigger: An in-memory delegation credential with a synthetic credential ID is rendered without a populated delegationCredentialId.

raw_findings.body: The deleted credential continues to display its old last-updated timestamp and delete action until the page is reloaded or another refetch occurs.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The mutation succeeds on the server while the client remains stale and presents cache data that no longer exists.
raw_findings.impact: The deleted credential continues to display its old last-updated timestamp and delete action until the page is reloaded or another refetch occurs.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new delete mutation relies on an optional parent callback and does not invalidate the query it changes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Invalidate or refetch `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the delete mutation's success or settled handler, independently of the optional callback.
raw_findings.title: Invalidate connected-calendar data after deleting cache
raw_findings.trigger: The dropdown is used without an `onSuccess` callback, or the callback does not refetch `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, and the user successfully deletes the cache.

raw_findings.body: Every legacy row is reported as having been updated at migration time, so the new cache-status UI shows a recent and incorrect last-updated timestamp.
raw_findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();
raw_findings.failure_mode: User-visible cache freshness data is silently rewritten to the migration time.
raw_findings.impact: Every legacy row is reported as having been updated at migration time, so the new cache-status UI shows a recent and incorrect last-updated timestamp.
raw_findings.root_cause: The required historical timestamp is initialized with the deployment clock rather than a value derived from each existing cache record.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add the column in a nullable or staged migration, backfill legacy timestamps from the existing expiry/cache lifetime where possible, then enforce the non-null default for future rows.
raw_findings.title: Backfill legacy cache timestamps instead of using migration time
raw_findings.trigger: The migration runs against existing CalendarCache rows that were created before `updatedAt` existed.

raw_findings.body: The script reads or creates the parent directory's `.env` instead of the repository's `.env`, so the web application does not receive the updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The script reports a successful environment update while modifying the wrong file.
raw_findings.impact: The script reads or creates the parent directory's `.env` instead of the repository's `.env`, so the web application does not receive the updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
raw_findings.root_cause: The script uses the caller's current working directory rather than its own location for a repository-relative path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Build `ENV_FILE` from the script's own directory, such as `SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd); ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env"`.
raw_findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
raw_findings.trigger: A developer runs the executable from the repository root, for example `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`.

raw_findings.body: GNU sed treats the empty backup argument as a filename and fails to update the environment file; because the script lacks `set -e`, it still prints the success message.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Webhook testing continues with the old URL while claiming the configuration was updated.
raw_findings.impact: GNU sed treats the empty backup argument as a filename and fails to update the environment file; because the script lacks `set -e`, it still prints the success message.
raw_findings.root_cause: The update command uses BSD/macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax in a Bash script without error handling.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a temporary file for the replacement or select the appropriate `sed -i` syntax based on the platform.
raw_findings.title: Use a portable in-place sed invocation
raw_findings.trigger: The script runs on Linux with an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL entry.

raw_findings.body: There is no added regression test ensuring that cross-user requests are rejected and that the other user's CalendarCache rows remain untouched for this destructive mutation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A regression in credential ownership checks can merge without automated coverage detecting unauthorized cache deletion.
raw_findings.impact: There is no added regression test ensuring that cross-user requests are rejected and that the other user's CalendarCache rows remain untouched for this destructive mutation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new destructive endpoint introduces an authorization branch without accompanying tests for its security boundary.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add handler tests covering successful deletion for the owner, rejection for a credential owned by another user, and preservation of that credential's cache rows.
raw_findings.title: Add authorization regression coverage for cache deletion
raw_findings.trigger: A future change alters the ownership predicate while handling a request containing another user's credential ID.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 9 shows 'ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()'. This sets all existing rows' updatedAt to migration execution time rather than actual last-update time. The UI displays cacheUpdatedAt (line 92 in CredentialActionsDropdown), so legacy rows will show misleading recent timestamps. Impact is user-visible incorrect data.

validated_findings.body: The script reads or creates the parent directory's `.env` instead of the repository's `.env`, so the web application does not receive the updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The script reports a successful environment update while modifying the wrong file.
validated_findings.impact: The script reads or creates the parent directory's `.env` instead of the repository's `.env`, so the web application does not receive the updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
validated_findings.root_cause: The script uses the caller's current working directory rather than its own location for a repository-relative path.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Build `ENV_FILE` from the script's own directory, such as `SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd); ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env"`.
validated_findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
validated_findings.trigger: A developer runs the executable from the repository root, for example `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 5 shows ENV_FILE="../.env" which is relative to CWD not script location. If run from repo root as ./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, CWD is repo root, so ../.env points to parent of repo. The script is a developer utility so impact is limited but the bug is real and the fix suggestion is correct.

validated_findings.body: GNU sed treats the empty backup argument as a filename and fails to update the environment file; because the script lacks `set -e`, it still prints the success message.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Webhook testing continues with the old URL while claiming the configuration was updated.
validated_findings.impact: GNU sed treats the empty backup argument as a filename and fails to update the environment file; because the script lacks `set -e`, it still prints the success message.
validated_findings.root_cause: The update command uses BSD/macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax in a Bash script without error handling.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a temporary file for the replacement or select the appropriate `sed -i` syntax based on the platform.
validated_findings.title: Use a portable in-place sed invocation
validated_findings.trigger: The script runs on Linux with an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL entry.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 68 shows 'sed -i '' -E' which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux, -i '' is interpreted as backup suffix argument, causing sed to fail or behave unexpectedly. The script lacks set -e (line 1 shows only #!/bin/bash), so failure is silent and line 73 prints success message regardless. Real portability bug.

validated_findings.body: There is no added regression test ensuring that cross-user requests are rejected and that the other user's CalendarCache rows remain untouched for this destructive mutation.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A regression in credential ownership checks can merge without automated coverage detecting unauthorized cache deletion.
validated_findings.impact: There is no added regression test ensuring that cross-user requests are rejected and that the other user's CalendarCache rows remain untouched for this destructive mutation.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new destructive endpoint introduces an authorization branch without accompanying tests for its security boundary.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add handler tests covering successful deletion for the owner, rejection for a credential owned by another user, and preservation of that credential's cache rows.
validated_findings.title: Add authorization regression coverage for cache deletion
validated_findings.trigger: A future change alters the ownership predicate while handling a request containing another user's credential ID.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test gap observation, not a bug in the patch. The handler at lines 17-22 correctly checks userId ownership before deletion. Absence of tests is a quality concern but not a defect introduced by the patch. The authorization logic itself is correct.
